title: Could have given that address too
html_source:
More implicature in the internal narrative continuing the single phrase enigmatic suspense of “Calypso”.

‘Bloom reflects that he could have used this post office as a blind in addition to the one in Westland Row towards which he is circling’ (Gifford, Ulysses Annotated: Notes for James Joyce’s Ulysses, p. 85).

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: I love this observation, which is to do with one of the most challenging and yet rewarding things about reading Ulysses …

But perhaps there are some clearer ways of putting it. “Implicature” is actually quite a specific term in the study of linguistics (esp. what you might call “pragmatic” linguistics) and while I understand the point, I think, I’m not sure it’s the most illuminating way to frame it.

Please disagree with me; I am very wiling to have my understanding of linguistic terms argued over. I have no real idea, for instance, whether other Joyce commentators have specifically discussed “implicature” w/r/t Ulysses.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: What is the resolution?
